title: Janus Engine — biomimetic oxygen extraction and closed phase-change thermal architecture
scope: Research branch for a biomimetic engine architecture combining dissolved-oxygen extraction inspired by fish gills, a reversible oxygen-carrier path, a physically separate oxygen delivery channel, and a closed internal phase-change cooling loop with an integrated condenser. This record defines hypotheses, invariants and validation gates; it does not claim a working engine or perpetual/self-sustaining cooling.

concept_sequence: fish gill extracts dissolved molecular oxygen through a thin high-area exchange surface
blood analog should transport oxygen reversibly rather than merely act as a passive liquid
oxygen path and thermal path remain physically separated
engine waste heat evaporates an internal working fluid
vapor is returned to liquid in an integrated ring condenser
a colder oxygen channel may pass through or alongside the condenser and contribute to local heat removal through the temperature gradient without mixing with the vapor
condensate returns to the hot zone, closing the working-fluid mass loop

architecture.physical_form: Concentric / gyroscopic ring architecture around a central working core. The initial 3D-printed form study supplied by the user is treated as a geometry reference, not as a functional pressure or thermal component.

nominal_flow: reversible oxygen carrier or facilitated-transport layer
cold or cool oxygen delivery channel

candidate_carrier_classes.hemoglobin_or_heme_analogs: High biomimetic similarity; stability and oxidation control unresolved.
candidate_carrier_classes.metal_porhyrin_or_related_reversible_com: Candidate facilitated oxygen carriers; selection and compatibility unresolved.
candidate_carrier_classes.perfluorocarbon_carriers: Candidate physical oxygen-solubility carrier; does not bind oxygen like hemoglobin.

possible_return_mechanisms: thermosiphon / gravity return where orientation permits

integrated_condenser.geometry_hypothesis: Ring or multi-ring condenser integrated directly into the engine body, potentially using hollow thin-wall channels rather than solid structural rings.
integrated_condenser.oxygen_channel_role: A colder oxygen stream may run inside a separate thermally conductive channel while vapor condenses on an adjacent external or annular surface. Any enhancement exists only to the extent that the oxygen stream can actually absorb heat.
integrated_condenser.external_sink: Final excess heat must be rejected to surrounding water, air, hull heat exchanger, or another colder reservoir.

biomimetic_mapping.blood: reversible oxygen carrier / facilitated transport medium
biomimetic_mapping.circulation: carrier loop or oxygen transport channel
biomimetic_mapping.thermoregulation: closed phase-change thermal loop plus external heat rejection

key_physics.oxygen_transfer: Driven by oxygen chemical-potential / partial-pressure gradients and membrane transport; the membrane does not need to mechanically trap O2 molecules.
key_physics.condensation_condition: Condensation occurs when the condensing surface is sufficiently below the saturation/dew-point temperature of the vapor at the local pressure.
key_physics.phase_change_heat: The thermal loop may transport large heat flux using latent heat of vaporization/condensation.
key_physics.heat_balance: At steady state, heat generated minus useful work must equal heat rejected to an external sink plus any stored/transient heat.
key_physics.oxygen_energy_constraint: Dissolved oxygen concentration in water is low; required water throughput and extraction efficiency may dominate system feasibility.

H1_artificial_gill.claim: A sufficiently high-area membrane and carrier architecture can continuously extract useful dissolved oxygen from flowing water.
H1_artificial_gill.falsification_gate: Measured oxygen extraction rate is insufficient for the intended engine load after accounting for pump power and membrane losses.

H2_closed_thermal_mass_loop.claim: A two-phase working fluid can circulate from hot core to condenser and return as liquid without routine loss of working fluid.
H2_closed_thermal_mass_loop.falsification_gate: Condensation or return rate cannot match evaporation rate across the intended operating envelope.

H3_oxygen_assisted_condensation.claim: A colder oxygen delivery channel can provide useful additional condenser heat removal before the oxygen reaches the engine.
H3_oxygen_assisted_condensation.falsification_gate: Oxygen mass flow, heat capacity and inlet temperature yield negligible cooling compared with condenser load or create unacceptable pressure losses.

H4_integrated_ring_engine.claim: Concentric or gyroscopic ring channels can integrate oxygen transport, vapor condensation and heat rejection compactly around a central engine core.
H4_integrated_ring_engine.falsification_gate: Thermal resistance, structural mass, flow resistance, sealing or manufacturability erase the compactness advantage.

first_principles_gates.G0_mass_energy_model: Build a complete steady-state mass and energy balance before combustion or high-temperature prototype work.
first_principles_gates.G1_dissolved_oxygen_budget: Measure or bound dissolved-O2 concentration, extraction fraction, water throughput, oxygen flow and pumping power.
first_principles_gates.G2_carrier_gate: Select and characterize carrier capacity, loading/unloading kinetics, regeneration energy, stability and membrane compatibility.
first_principles_gates.G3_condenser_gate: Demonstrate condensation capacity with a safe dummy heat source and separate cold channel; measure heat flux and pressure drop.
first_principles_gates.G4_closed_loop_gate: Demonstrate repeated evaporation-condensation-return cycles without meaningful working-fluid loss or dryout.
first_principles_gates.G5_coupled_gate: Couple oxygen transport and thermal loop only after both work independently.
first_principles_gates.G6_engine_gate: Only after previous gates pass, evaluate whether available oxygen flow and heat rejection support a useful engine or fuel-cell load.

steps: test ring condenser geometry using a controlled electric dummy heater rather than a combustion engine
test the closed phase-change loop separately from oxygen extraction
test artificial-gill oxygen extraction separately and measure actual O2 flow
test a separate cool gas channel through the condenser and quantify its incremental heat-removal contribution
combine subsystems only after measured budgets close

safety_boundary.oxygen: Oxygen-enriched gas near hot surfaces, oils, seals and polymers can greatly increase ignition and fire severity; oxygen-compatible materials and strict physical separation are mandatory design considerations.
safety_boundary.pressure: Steam, vapor and gas loops can become pressurized; the 3D-printed form study is not a pressure vessel.
safety_boundary.temperature: High-temperature engine testing is outside the scope of this registry root entry.
safety_boundary.unknown_carriers: No candidate oxygen carrier is authorized for human, animal, medical or breathing-gas use by this record.
safety_boundary.prototype_rule: Early validation should use low-energy, instrumented thermal and flow experiments rather than an oxygen-enriched combustion prototype.

success_definition.thermal: Stable closed working-fluid circulation with condenser capacity at least equal to evaporator vapor generation over the target load range.
success_definition.oxygen: Measured net oxygen extraction sufficient for the target conversion core after subtracting parasitic pumping/separation power.
success_definition.system: Combined system closes measured mass and energy balances and rejects unavoidable waste heat to an identified external sink.

next_gate: JANUS_ENGINE_G0_MASS_ENERGY_MODEL: calculate oxygen demand, dissolved-O2 water throughput, carrier capacity, thermal load, condenser area and parasitic pumping power for a defined target output before selecting the final engine type.
